biur-halacha/1:_: While it is still day — know that what Rama wrote in the gloss "close to bein hashemashot" is not the Mechaber's view but his own view, as explained in Darkei Moshe; but for the Mechaber it is permitted l'chatchila to draw by day at any hour he wishes, provided he waits to knead with them until the morrow, as his view is explained in Beit Yosef; and so Gra, Peri Chadash, and Maamar Mordechai ruled as the main view; therefore Maamar Mordechai wrote that where there is some pressure one may fill by day while the day is still long, since according to Maran, may he rest in Eden, one may do so l'chatchila.
biur-halacha/3:א: Large kettle — see Mishna Berurah for the reason; see Peri Megadim that this applies only when the cauldron is still somewhat lukewarm from having been moved from the fire a short time ago; if it cooled a long time, obviously there is no concern.
biur-halacha/3:ג: One may rely on them — Beit Chadash is stringent in all cases; but many acharonim wrote like Shulchan Aruch and Rama; and even according to Beit Chadash, if drawn from rivers one may rely to be lenient b'dieved b'shogeg, for it is known that according to Rashi the main law of water not left overnight applies specifically to springs; and likewise in mayim shelanu that were hot and one cooled them b'shogeg — one may be lenient even per Beit Chadash; and so Eliyah Rabbah.
biur-halacha/5:_: It is customary, etc., and this is correct — from this language it implies only l'chatchila but b'dieved one does not forbid; and therefore they did not decide that a little salt put in matzah for taste would heat the dough [for although we rule salted is like boiling, that is specifically when it is not eaten because of its salt], and he was not concerned for the stringent authorities only regarding l'chatchila; and Rama in the gloss who added to forbid even b'dieved follows his reasoning, for Darkei Moshe wrote that according to what Tur wrote later siman 462, salt water is fruit juice — if so it is fruit juice with water, and we rule they hasten to leaven unless baked immediately; therefore he wrote here that even b'dieved it is forbidden — meaning if he was not careful to bake immediately [and the dough in his hands does not save from leavening]; and so Kaf HaChayim ruled [and so implies Magen Avraham]: if he was careful to bake immediately, one does not forbid b'dieved the matzah for a little salt put in; and so Eliyah Rabbah. Know that according to what Rama wrote later siman 462 in Darkei Moshe, Tur deals only with salt dug from the ground, but salt made from sea water like mayim shelanu is water for everyone — if so one does not forbid b'dieved in our salt in any case (unless he put much salt), and even per Magen Avraham's objection there that Tur deals with our salt — nevertheless for the law Beit Yosef concludes there in the name of Ran and Hagahot Maimoniyot unlike Tur, and so ruled in Shulchan Aruch that it is in the category of water; if so Rama's ruling to forbid even b'dieved applies only to salt dug from the ground if not baked immediately. Know further that even if we explain Rama in Shulchan Aruch who ruled anonymously to be stringent b'dieved, it is not because it is fruit juice but because he was concerned for the stringent view due to heating the dough — nevertheless for the law one should study, for many poskim are lenient as Gra wrote; and so is proven in Ritva's novellae on Pesachim that b'dieved one certainly should not be stringent with a little salt; and so Maharam Chalavah in his novellae to be lenient with little salt. Especially if he was shogeg, one certainly should not be stringent, for even kneading in hot water some poskim are lenient b'shogeg b'dieved as above seif 3 — all the more so here where many are certainly lenient one may rely — in my humble opinion. See Peri Chadash who disagrees with Rama and agrees with Mechaber to be lenient b'dieved.
chatam-sofer/1:_: (There in Taz s.k. 3) "He who keeps a mitzvah," etc. And that he did not bring this verse in the chapter Erev Pesachim daf 109b — because the rabbis would not institute a new mitzvah and rely on this, as Semak wrote siman 67 s.k. 2 in such a case — see there.
chatam-sofer/2:_: In Mechaber seif 5 in the gloss "one should forbid" — Mishna Berurah; see my responsa part 6 Orach Chayim siman 123.
chok-yaakov/1:א: Or at bein hashemashot. The main time to draw is between sunset and nightfall before the moon shines on the ground — so too Maharil; see above siman 261 for the measure of bein hashemashot. Since not everyone knows how to measure bein hashemashot, one draws close to bein hashemashot after sunset. B'dieved, if drawn while it is still day or drawn after the beginning of the night, it appears from the later authorities one may be lenient to knead with them after 12 hours. In responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 he wrote one should not be lenient unless in a time of pressure or great loss — see above seif 3. See Taz who wrote it is better after drawing than before. However Maharil wrote the opposite — end quote: it is better to draw a little early than to delay, for overnight standing is not mentioned explicitly in the Talmud — end quote; his words appear correct and so implies Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/1:ג: And when carrying water under the open sky. This refers to the above that he wrote it is good to place them under the ceiling so that if he forgets to bring them in at dawn the sun will not shine on them. Therefore he also wrote: be careful also when carrying water by day under the open sky to the kneading house to cover it with a cloth so they will not become warm, as Semag and Semak wrote and Terumat HaDeshen siman 115 explicitly; and so Levush explained it deals by day — in the evening hour when they draw, since the sun already set, one need not cover them at all; it is only custom and extra caution lest something heating fall in, as Terumat HaDeshen wrote there. All this is simple and clear, unlike Magen Avraham who explained it refers to the time of drawing.
chok-yaakov/1:ה: Eve of the 13th, meaning Thursday night. For on Thursday night one is concerned lest he draw before Friday sunset or delay and violate Shabbos — so is the language of Mordechai end of the first chapter of Pesachim; from this it is implied b'dieved if he forgot to draw on the night of the 13th he may draw on Friday while it is still day close to bein hashemashot or even at bein hashemashot, for we are not concerned for Shabbos violation, for anything that is due to shevut they did not decree against at bein hashemashot in a place of mitzvah, as explained above siman 261 and Shaarei Teshuvah there. However from Rokeach siman 265 and as brought by later authorities who wrote: when the 14th falls on Shabbos they draw on the night of the 13th from the river or well and do not draw from the cistern in his courtyard on Shabbos for kneading because he needs much and it appears like filling his garden and ruin as in Eruvin 104 — end quote — it appears that even b'dieved drawing is forbidden; and in truth Rokeach's words seem astonishing, for what prohibition is there, since it appears like filling — for there it is explained specifically via a wheel it is forbidden because he draws much and draws easily; and even with our wheel some permit as explained above siman 338 seif 16 — all the more so what they draw now for an individual in his house one or two buckets, which is a small matter, and also at bein hashemashot where they did not decree shevut. If so, what prohibition is there? Rokeach's words can be answered with difficulty that his intent is if he wants to draw on Shabbos itself, as somewhat implied in his language, and not at bein hashemashot; and it deals when they want to draw much for the courtyard — but not when forgotten for an individual, permitted to draw one or two buckets in his courtyard at bein hashemashot or even in the river where carrying is permitted (however from later authorities who brought Rokeach it does not imply so). More plausible is concern for preparing from Shabbos to Yom Tov: (found in Shaarei Teshuvah siman 7 permission via small vessels and many people for this reason does not help). This concern is also in Beit Yosef and Magen Avraham, and they conclude one who forgot to draw on the night of the 5th should draw on Friday while it is still day, or command a gentile at bein hashemashot, or take water drawn in his house even if not drawn for the mitzvah since impossible otherwise — end quote; and it is better to draw oneself or via agent that day close to bein hashemashot where there is no prohibition concern like other ways — see above s.k. 1 and responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 who wrote: the custom spread not to knead matzah after Shabbos except with water drawn on the eve of the 6th, for one can limit drawing at bein hashemashot unlike two bein hashemashot of Erev Shabbos; and what he wrote: where there is custom one should not be lenient unless pressure or great loss — end quote; nevertheless where there is no custom one should not be stringent and should not act as he wrote.
chok-yaakov/1:ו: To draw from wells. Maharil wrote: it is a good custom first to clean and purify the spring; and if impossible to clean all of it because of many water sources, nevertheless draw much water from it before drawing. And all cisterns in houses — generally much water was drawn in them to clean vessels for Pesach days — end quote; and in Shaarei Knesset HaGedolah: our custom is to filter water through a white cloth so nothing falls in — end quote. All this is only stringency l'chatchila — see above siman 457 s.k. 12 and siman 467 seif 12.
chok-yaakov/1:ז: Nevertheless l'chatchila it is good to place iron in them. Take new iron and hang it on a rope — Maharil and later authorities. Magen Avraham wrote in Darkei Moshe in the name of Hagahot Maimoniyot: on all other days of the year one places salt or a seal — end quote. Taz wrote: nevertheless it appears that on other nights if he did not place iron to guard from tekufah he may discard them if he can easily be without those waters, unlike these waters of matzah of the mitzvah where it is forbidden to discard, for it appears contemptuous of the verse "He who keeps a mitzvah knows no evil" — end quote; and similarly Maharshal in his explanation to Semag; and the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek objected that his words imply only matzah of the mitzvah permits keeping the water, but even for other matzot one need not be particular about tekufah if one died; nevertheless he concludes in the name of Agudah that even for matzah of the mitzvah one permits only when impossible to borrow mayim shelanu in that city. It appears simple that even Agudah who is stringent speaks only in a small city with few people, but in a large city one is certainly not obligated to go door to door for water, only among neighbors and acquaintances — and so implies Taz's language that even all year one should not be stringent if he cannot easily be without that water — all the more so these waters; and the custom is to be lenient in every regard.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: Also forbidden for a gentile to draw. That is l'chatchila; and so explicit in Maharil that it is extra stringency l'chatchila; and so Shlah.
chok-yaakov/1:ט: And it is customary to take designated water. One says at the time of drawing for the sake of the mitzvah of matzah — Maharil and Mahariv siman 193; and Maharil wrote further that some take designated water each night independently.
chok-yaakov/1:י: New earthenware vessels, etc. All books of Shulchan Aruch wrote so in the name of Kol Bo but I did not find it in his words. Magen Avraham wrote: Maggid Mishneh wrote one should not take a vessel that had fruit juice, for fruit juice with water hastens leavening (and it appears permitted through hagalah). Also one should not take a copper vessel that heats — end quote; however I have seen people knead in copper troughs — end quote Magen Avraham. In truth one can distinguish: mayim shelanu require cooling, and in copper they may not cool — unlike for kneading; see Hagahot Minhagim who also forbids drawing in copper, and so is customary; b'dieved one does not forbid — and so Ateret Zekenim siman 266; and so appears from what is written seif 3 regarding thick copper.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: Unless in a time of pressure. If he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house he should take them even if there is concern they were drawn by day or at night; see Beit Yosef and R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Bach siman 7; see what is written above s.k. 1 and s.k. 5 in the name of Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/3:א: One may not knead in hot water. Levush wrote: even if left overnight all night and heated only by the sun — thus his intent: even mayim shelanu, as long as they are still hot, it is forbidden to knead with them; unlike if they are cold before us, for which overnight water is needed to remove heat from the sun, as explained in the Talmud and poskim; and the same for copper-kettle water if cooled, as poskim and Mechaber imply who wrote "and water inside is lukewarm" — specifically while still lukewarm. However in responsum of Rama siman 35 he wrote: copper-kettle water, even after cooling, should be forbidden, for an intentional transgressor — not to mention R' Eliezer of Metz, for even water not left overnight, cooling does not help — all the more so hot water; and even per Rashi in copper-kettle water there is no remedy; therefore we do not find any posek who wrote there is remedy for copper-kettle water — end quote. In truth the Mechaber's implication is not so — see Ateret Zekenim; and so the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek from Mahari Weil; the poskim did not need to write remedy because copper-kettle water is stated, and whatever cooled is no longer copper-kettle water; and since they are cold before us, what prohibition is there — and on the contrary I have heard that sometimes water that was boiled and cooled is colder than other water. What he wrote that for R' Eliezer of Metz cooling does not help for water not left overnight is not necessary — see Beit Yosef. Although Mahari Weil that the brother-in-law brought concludes: heaven forbid to contradict their words without proof — it appears he understood Levush's "even if left overnight" means even if cooled; therefore he did not come to contradict his words. In truth Levush's intent is simple as written; and proof is clear from Talmud and poskim and Mechaber who wrote specifically hot or lukewarm; one who wants to be stringent in any case has permission to permit b'dieved.
chok-yaakov/3:ב: That its copper is thick. Magen Avraham wrote: the same applies to earthenware.
chok-yaakov/3:ג: Lukewarm. That is, like the warmth of saliva; and it is in Yerushalmi end of chapter Kol Sha'ah halachah 7: although in Menachot they knead in lukewarm water and guard lest it leaven because priests are zealous — in matzah even priests themselves should not knead in lukewarm water so there is no distinction between matzah and matzah — end quote; see Menachot 55a; and explained in Tur and Beit Yosef that in benefit everyone permits even kneading in hot water.
chok-yaakov/4:_: One in two. It implies specifically one in two; see Sefer Me'irat Einayim general rule 91 s.k. 6; see Magen Avraham; and it is implied from poskim brought in Beit Yosef that if mixed during kneading it is not nullified — we require specifically mixed before kneading. The rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek raised b'dieved to permit even in such a case — see above s.k. 16; Magen Avraham wrote permitted to mix them even l'chatchila to cool them — requires study; and the same for copper-kettle water this cooling helps according to all — so Ateret Zekenim; see s.k. 13. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape matzot faces with salt water and return to the oven as on Chol HaMoed; specifically on Chol HaMoed permitted to scrape, but on the first two nights forbidden (Ateret Zekenim).
chok-yaakov/5:_: One should forbid. That is in eating; but in benefit certainly permitted, for Mishna Berurah compared it to kneading in hot water. If he put a little salt, if baked immediately permitted in eating — end quote; and all this if kneaded with water; but if kneaded with fruit juice, Bach ruled one should not forbid b'dieved.
chok-yaakov/6:א: Valid. Nevertheless one does not fulfill the obligation of matzah with it and one does not eat it on the first night as rich matzah, since according to many poskim one fulfills with it — see above siman 462 and 471.
chok-yaakov/6:ב: And pepper. Magen Avraham wrote even one grain forbids; specifically when kneaded into it; but if it fell on it one removes it and it is permitted; ginger is treated like pepper; possibly the same for anise and saffron — end quote; the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek ruled to permit in eating all kinds of spices; and so appears to me primary, for poskim mentioned only pepper; and they say: good is sharp pepper — Aruch explains because it is sharper than all spices; if so one should not compare other spices; and even in pepper one forbids only in eating like salt, as s.k. 18; and so Bach and Ateret Zekenim — they are equal.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] Bein hashemashot, etc. Or close to bein hashemashot (Rama). Bach wrote: if drawn while it was still day and left overnight, or drawn after the beginning of the night and left overnight, it is permitted even l'chatchila — until here. It appears to me specifically before midnight; but after midnight it is forbidden, for we rely on Semak that overnight standing is from midnight until dawn — and he was precise and wrote "after the beginning of the night." Also it appears to me that after dawn it is permitted immediately even though not yet twelve hours from drawing — and so Bach end of siman 4 explicitly; Chak Yaakov did not understand so. Semak wrote in Hagahot: it is proper to wait to knead until the day brightens much lest one err by moonlight.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] And when carrying, etc., under the air, etc. Requires study: if it deals with kneading, he already wrote at the end of the seif; if when drawing, he wrote one need not cover them. Perhaps here it deals at night when he wants to place them in an open place he should cover, for then he might forget tomorrow — no concern. People always leave them covered at night even under the ceiling, and we are not concerned they will heat from this covering; the reason appears to me we are concerned something might fall in; and although Terumat HaDeshen wrote this is extra caution, it appears that is when carrying from river to house while engaged with it; but where they stand all night there is more concern.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] One may knead only with mayim shelanu — even matzah that is not for the mitzvah, because of concern for leavening. Rashbatz in Maamar Chametz daf 30 and responsa part 2 siman 87; brought by Birkei Yosef note 1, Kissei Eliyahu note 1, Shaarei Teshuvah siman 7. And so Rosh end of chapter Kol Sha'ah and Maggid Mishneh chapter 5 law 11; Beit David, Beit Yosef. And so Kolbo 38a that the geonim and majority of scholars agreed, not like R' Yitzchak Giat — see there; Beit David Hagah note 1; and so Raz note 1.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There. One may knead only with mayim shelanu. Doubtful mayim shelanu — one should not knead with them; if he kneaded, permitted. Mahari Bueno — brought by Rav Mezbeach Adamah; see what Morenu, may he rest in Eden, wrote in the gloss seif 3 from Mechaber in Kuntres Acharon note 1.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (4) One who collected rainwater — permitted to knead matzah with it and no overnight standing is required according to all, provided he does not leave them where their coldness will dissipate. Radbaz part 5 siman 2002; brought by Birkei Yosef note 4, Shaarei Teshuvah note 9. However Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 97 distinguishes: if collected by day requires overnight; if collected at night no overnight required — see there; brought by Yad Aharon in Hagahot and Birkei Yosef there; see further below note 64 what is written on this — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (5) Permitted to knead with water a gentile said offhandedly is ours in his house, for prohibition is not presumed and it is rabbinic; one who is stringent — tavo le-olam. Rav HaChasid Mahari Molcho, may he rest in Eden, responsa part 1 siman 103; Birkei Yosef note 5. It appears one certainly does not fulfill the mitzvot with these, for there is no guarding; and for other matzot also one should be concerned lest something leavening fell in and the like; in a time of pressure one may permit through filtering — Shaarei Teshuvah there.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There. One may knead only with mayim shelanu — meaning ours in another vessel after drawing. Rashi explained (Pesachim 42a): because in Nissan days the springs are hot since the rainy season still applies, and in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower sky; therefore the whole world is cold and springs hot; therefore we leave overnight and they cool — end quote. Some explain the reason: because at night the sun travels under the earth and heats the springs; therefore their only remedy is not to be attached at night, as Beit Yosef explains — see there. In derashot of Maharil he wrote the water must cool 24 hours before kneading: 12 hours by day while attached in the well when the sun is far, and 12 hours at night after drawing — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: And Rashi — we rule like R' Nachman there 94b: in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower sky; therefore the whole world is cold and springs boil. Rashi there: in the lower part of the sky, close to the ground, at the edges of the sphere; therefore the whole world is cold, for it travels only at the sides of the world; and springs boil — meaning near the water at the sides of the world from which springs come — end quote. Nissan is still considered rainy season. Therefore there is no difference between night and day — always in rainy season, day and night, it travels in the lower sky; only at night it travels in the vault of the sky and the sky separates between sun and earth, hence darkness on the earth; by day it travels in the hollow of the sky toward the earth, hence the earth is lit. Therefore no difference whether drawn by day or night — water is hot and needs 12 hours cooling; if drawn in the morning, permitted to knead with them in the evening after 12 hours. R' Yehuda uses mayim shelanu implying they draw in the evening and knead in the morning — common practice: people bake by day, therefore must leave all night and may bake immediately at dawn.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ג: And R' Eliezer of Metz — we rule like the admission of the sages of Israel to the sages of the nations there: no difference between summer and rainy season; always by day it travels below the sky (therefore it lights for us), and at night below the ground (therefore earth's thickness separates between sun and us, hence night darkens); therefore by day springs cold, at night boiling — at night the sun travels near the place springs issue; by day when the sun is far they cool. According to him, if drawn at bein hashemashot, permitted to knead immediately, for they already cooled 12 hours attached by day. In this there is no dispute per R' Eliezer of Metz — only if drawn by day or night they disagree: R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Rabbeinu Yehuda — per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi whether drawn day or night they have no remedy forever. Rabbeinu Yehuda challenged: if so why call them mayim shelanu? In any case if drawn at bein hashemashot no overnight needed and permitted immediately; if drawn by day or night, overnight does not help — therefore Rabbeinu Yehuda: per R' Eliezer of Metz, if drawn by day they need overnight of the following night and it helps; if drawn at night they need the full night they were drawn and the day after and the night after. His reason and reasoning — see Beit Yosef who elaborated greatly. R' Yitzchak Saba's view is also like R' Eliezer of Metz here, for we rule like admission of sages of Israel; except where R' Eliezer of Metz holds if drawn at bein hashemashot no overnight needed because they cooled 12 hours attached — R' Yitzchak Saba disagrees and requires 24 hours cooling; therefore draw at bein hashemashot; then they cool 12 hours attached by day (for by day springs are cold) and need overnight all night and cool 12 hours detached (for at night the world is cold). Maharil leans like R' Yitzchak Saba. One should not be lenient to draw by day (meaning before close to bein hashemashot, about half hour before) — per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it is not correct; meaning per R' Eliezer of Metz not correct per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi even if left all night, for they have no remedy; but per Rabbeinu Yehuda overnight of the night helps as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ד: In this all agree. Meaning R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Rabbeinu Yehuda agree it is not correct per R' Eliezer of Metz to draw at night; they disagree: per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi they have no remedy forever; per Rabbeinu Yehuda overnight of the night drawn does not help; nevertheless overnight of the following night helps as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ו: One may be lenient: first, one may rely on Rashi that 12 hours waiting suffices whether drawn by day or night as above; second, even R' Eliezer of Metz was stringent only l'chatchila when possible; when impossible, perhaps R' Eliyahu Mizrachi agrees to be lenient.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ז: Know Bach wrote further leniency per Raavan who holds for Rashi one does not need 12 hours at night but suffices until after dawn if the night was short. Authors ruled 12 hours for Rashi — fixed time by day if drawn in morning; in Nissan day and night are equal and night is 12 hours; therefore its measure by day equals places where in Nissan night is 12 hours — because we do not distinguish. But if drawn at evening bein hashemashot, leaving the night as it is, even if short, permitted immediately at dawn — I copied his words to be a shield for people of the land who do not wait 12 hours and knead at dawn — they have whom to rely on; but most poskim did not write so and one should not be lenient. See siman 261 measure of bein hashemashot; Magen Avraham wrote there it is about a quarter hour — see there; see here Taz s.v. regarding law, etc.; see Kaf HaChayim agreed with Magen Avraham that better to draw a little before bein hashemashot than after — unlike Taz.
machatzit-hashekel/4:א: (s.k. 4) On the night of the 5th, etc. Explanation: for those who bake, etc. — meaning it is explained siman 458: when Pesach falls on Sunday one kneads Friday evening after chatzot; obviously one draws Thursday night. Rama needed to write this for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos, as Tur siman 458.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ג: See siman 7 one may rely on Rabbeinu Yehuda — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ה: See siman 307: shevut of shevut is permitted in a place of mitzvah; therefore permitted to command a gentile.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ו: And siman 464 — meaning although Rama wrote in this seif forbidden via gentile; he brought proof from siman 464 that kneading and baking are certainly forbidden via gentile, yet Magen Avraham wrote there when impossible otherwise permitted via gentile when Jew stands over — all the more so drawing. Or take water drawn in his house — meaning mayim shelanu even if not drawn for the mitzvah.
machatzit-hashekel/5:ב: But, etc. — always boiling; therefore wells are preferable.
magen-avraham/1:א: Close to bein hashemashot. By right one should draw at bein hashemashot itself so water cools 12 hours attached by day when springs are cold, and 12 hours in the air at night as Maharil wrote; but since impossible to measure bein hashemashot precisely, permitted to draw close to bein hashemashot. One should not be lenient to draw by day, for per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it is not correct — all the more so not to draw at night, for in this all agree. Beit Yosef wrote: if drawn after beginning of night they have no remedy and the water is forbidden forever per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — end quote Darkei Moshe; Bach wrote b'dieved if drawn at night one may be lenient to knead by day; see siman 261 measure of bein hashemashot.
magen-avraham/1:ד: Thursday night. Explanation: for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos and cannot draw at Motzei Shabbos nor Friday when they need bein hashemashot and Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov — therefore draw Thursday night belonging to Friday (Beit Yosef); see siman 467; if so, also those baking on second day of Yom Tov forbidden to draw at bein hashemashot on Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need eve of 14th; see siman 458. It appears if he forgot Thursday night he may draw Friday while still day on this Erev Pesach, or command gentile at bein hashemashot — see siman 307 and 464; or take water drawn in his house even if not drawn for mitzvah since impossible otherwise.
magen-avraham/1:ח: Or falling tekufah. And Yoreh De'ah siman 116 wrote there is danger only when drinking at the hour tekufah falls (and so Shulchan Aruch HaRav).
magen-avraham/1:י: Wooden vessel, etc. — the same for glazed earthenware; see siman 473 seif 3.
magen-avraham/3:א: Large kettle. The copper of the kettle retains heat (Rashi); it does not deal with water heated on the fire, for then even if completely cooled it is forbidden even not in the cauldron — merely putting water in the cauldron without fire is forbidden because the cauldron retains heat; so Agur in his responsum (Rama siman 35).
magen-avraham/4:_: One in two. Implies less than that is not nullified (Beit Yosef); but Semag and Semak wrote nullified in majority, and so Yoreh De'ah siman 98; we rule see Ateret Zekenim; it appears permitted to mix them l'chatchila, for the reason is not prohibition but when not left overnight they are hot and when mixed they become cold; if so permitted to cool l'chatchila — requires study.
magen-avraham/5:_: One should forbid. Thus Darkei Moshe; and per his words siman 462, even b'dieved one should forbid; and so Mordechai: one who eats salted matzah is like eating chametz — end quote; it appears if a grain of salt fell in, bake immediately as siman 462; if due to heating one may rely on "all in it" that little salt does not heat; and b'dieved siman 91.
magen-avraham/6:ב: Since it has. Implies one fulfills with it on the first nights; however in Rambam it implies rich matzah; and so Maggid Mishneh chapter 6.
magen-avraham/6:ג: And pepper. Even one grain makes entire dough chametz; and same little lime (Darkei Moshe, Mahariv); appears specifically kneaded in; if fell on, remove and permitted; in hints it implies pepper permitted b'dieved; nevertheless do not be lenient — see above seif 5 regarding salt; appears ginger like pepper; possibly anise and saffron too.
